title: Getting around
goal: Ask for and understand directions, take buses, trains and autos, and tell a driver where to go.
intro: Getting around means giving instructions — so this unit teaches the **imperative**, in its informal and polite forms — and the case endings for **to** (-க்கு), **from** (-லேருந்து) and **up to** (-வரைக்கும்). You'll be negotiating with auto-rickshaw drivers in no time.

vocab.note: spoken: ஸ்டேஷன் sṭēshan; ரயில் நிலையம் 'railway station'

phrases.en: If I go this way, will I reach the temple?

phrases.native: இல்ல, பக்கம்தான். அஞ்சு நிமிஷம் நடந்தா போதும்.
phrases.roman: illa, pakkamdān. anju nimisham naḍandā pōdum.
phrases.en: No, it's close. Just a five-minute walk.
Does this bus go to Marina Beach?
Which stop should I get off at?

grammar.title: Imperatives: informal, polite and negative
grammar.body:
The **informal** command is the bare verb root (often with -உ added in speech): **வா** 'come', **போ** 'go', **சொல்லு** 'say', **பாரு** 'look'. Use it only with children and close friends.

The **polite** command adds **-ங்க** *-nga* (written -உங்கள்): **வாங்க, போங்க, சொல்லுங்க, பாருங்க, திரும்புங்க, உக்காருங்க**. Roots ending in a consonant add -உ- first (a single l doubles): சொல் → சொல்லுங்க, கேள் → கேளுங்க; roots ending in -உ just add -ங்க: நிறுத்து → நிறுத்துங்க, குடு → குடுங்க.

The **negative** command is infinitive/stem + **-ஆதே** (informal) or **-ஆதீங்க** (polite): போகாதே / போகாதீங்க 'don't go', சொல்லாதீங்க 'don't say'.

grammar.title: To, from, up to, by: direction cases
grammar.body:
Direction is shown by suffixes on the (oblique) noun:

**-க்கு** *-kku* — to: சென்னைக்கு 'to Chennai', வீட்டுக்கு 'home', கடைக்கு 'to the shop'
**-லேருந்து** *-lērundu* — from (written -இலிருந்து): மதுரைலேருந்து 'from Madurai'
**-வரைக்கும்** *-varaikkum* — up to, as far as: ஸ்டேஷன் வரைக்கும் 'up to the station'
**வழியா** *vaḻiyā* — via, through: பாலம் வழியா 'via the bridge'
**-ல** *-la* — by (vehicle): பஸ்ல 'by bus', ட்ரெயின்ல 'by train', ஆட்டோல 'by auto'

Note: Tamil uses the dative for 'to' even with 'go': நான் கடைக்குப் போறேன் 'I'm going to the shop' — though with common places like ஆஃபீஸ், ஸ்கூல் the -க்கு is often dropped in speech.

examples.en: I walked as far as the station.
Which way should I go to the beach?

dialogue.title: Taking an auto
dialogue.setting: Sarah flags down an auto-rickshaw in T. Nagar, Chennai.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: Brother, will you go to the Mylapore temple?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.en: I'll go, madam. A hundred and fifty rupees.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: நூத்தி ஐம்பதா? ரொம்ப ஜாஸ்தி! மீட்டர் போடுங்க.
lines.roman: nūtti aimbadā? romba jāsti! mīṭṭar pōḍunga.
lines.en: A hundred and fifty? That's too much! Put the meter on.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.native: மீட்டர் வேலை செய்யல மேடம். நூத்தி இருபது குடுங்க.
lines.roman: mīṭṭar vēlai seyyala mēḍam. nūtti irubadu kuḍunga.
lines.en: The meter doesn't work, madam. Give me a hundred and twenty.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.en: Don't worry, madam. Shall I stop at the temple entrance?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: இல்ல, அந்த மூலையில நிறுத்துங்க. நான் இறங்கிக்கிறேன்.
lines.roman: illa, anda mūlaiyila niruttunga. nān irangikkirēn.
lines.en: No, stop at that corner. I'll get off there.

culture: Auto-rickshaw fares are usually negotiated before you get in; ride-hailing apps have made this easier in cities. Calling the driver அண்ணா 'elder brother' is friendly and normal. Directions are typically given with landmarks rather than street names: 'turn left at the temple', 'next to the bank'. Many Chennai roads have both an official name and an older popular name.

tip.title: Polite commands: add -ங்க
tip.body:
- The bare verb is a command to a child or close friend: **போ** 'go', **திரும்பு** 'turn'.
- For everyone else add **-ங்க**: **போங்க**, **திரும்புங்க**, **சொல்லுங்க**.
- 'Don't' is **-ஆதீங்க**: **போகாதீங்க** 'don't go', **திரும்பாதீங்க** 'don't turn'.
- Directions go before the verb: இடது பக்கம் திரும்புங்க 'turn left'.

sentences.en: Go straight on.
Turn right at the corner.
After the bridge, turn left.
Don't turn there, go straight on.
Turn left, kiddo.
Don't go over the bridge.
Left or right?
I don't know the way.
Sir, I've lost my way.

lessons.title: Places in town

tip.title: Town words people really say
tip.body:
- Signs use the written words; in speech most places have an English name: வங்கி → **பேங்க்**, சாலை → **ரோடு**, சந்தை → **மார்க்கெட்**.
- **ஹோட்டல்** means any place to eat, not a hotel to sleep in. Written உணவகம்.
- Big roads keep சாலை in their names: **அண்ணா சாலை**.
- 'Is it far?' **தூரமா?** · 'It's close' **பக்கம்தான்**.

new: இல்ல, பக்கம்தான். அஞ்சு நிமிஷம் நடந்தா போதும்.

sentences.en: Is there a bank nearby?
Where is Indian Bank?
The bank is on the other side of the bridge.
There's a good place to eat on this road.
That restaurant is next to the temple.
The temple is right on this street.
The shop is on the corner.
That shop is on Anna Salai.
Is the market very far?
The market isn't far, it's close.
It's just a ten-minute walk.

lessons.title: By bus, by train, by car

tip.title: 'To' is -க்கு, 'by' is -ல
tip.body:
- Where you're going takes **-க்கு**: சென்னை**க்கு**, வீட்டு**க்கு**, கடை**க்கு**. Before ப the k doubles in writing: கடைக்குப் போறேன்.
- The vehicle takes **-ல**: பஸ்**ல** 'by bus', ட்ரெயின்**ல** 'by train', கார்**ல** 'by car'.
- Don't mix them up: -ல is also 'in, at', never 'to'.

sentences.en: I'm going by bus.
Tomorrow we're going to Chennai by train.
Dad goes to the office by car.
Shall we go by train?
How will you get home?
We can go on my scooter.
I'll pop to the shop and come back.
How do I get to the bus stand?
Two tickets, please.
How much is a train ticket?

lessons.title: Which stop do I get off at?

tip.title: From, as far as, via
tip.body:
- **-லேருந்து** = from: ஸ்டேஷன்**லேருந்து** 'from the station'.
- **வரைக்கும்** = up to, as far as: பாலம் **வரைக்கும்**.
- **வழியா** = via, through: கோவில் **வழியா**.
- Getting on is **ஏறு**, getting off **இறங்கு**; the stop takes -ல: இந்த ஸ்டாப்**ல** இறங்குங்க.

sentences.en: I'm coming from the station.
How far is home from the airport?
Which bus goes to the airport?
Get off at this stop.
Walk as far as the bridge.
Does this bus go as far as Central?
This bus goes via the bridge.
It's shorter if you go via the temple.
Get on quickly, the bus is leaving!
Get on at the front, get off at the back.

tip.title: Talking to the driver
tip.body:
- Call the driver **அண்ணா** 'brother': friendly and polite.
- Fix the price before you get in: **ஸ்டேஷனுக்கு எவ்வளவு?** or ask for the meter: **மீட்டர் போடுங்க**.
- To stop: **இங்க நிறுத்துங்க**; not here: **இங்க நிறுத்தாதீங்க**.
- Will you go? **வருவீங்களா?** (drivers think of it as 'coming' with you).

sentences.en: Brother, will you go to the station?
How much will it be to the airport?
Two hundred rupees? That's too much, brother.
Did you put the meter on?
Is there an auto stand nearby?
Get in the auto, I'll show you the way.
Stop in front of the temple, please.
Don't stop here, a bit further on.
I'll get off here.
